title: test_map reaches through res:// refs, tables and one class hop instead of FULL

body:
## Summary
test_map decides what `--changed` (and tools/mutate) runs by plain text mention. It sends 57% of real project-touching commits to the FULL suite, and on the other 43% it misses the tests of the changed file's direct dependents. Replace the mention check with a derived reach index built from res:// literals (including directory constants), class_name and autoload names, plus one dependent hop.

## Description
New `tools/tests/reach_index.mjs` builds, in one pass (~3 s, zero-dep), a reverse index over project/{boot,core,features,dev}: the files each res:// literal names (the exact path, else the nearest ancestor-directory literal), and class_name/autoload name -> declaring file. `mapChanges` keeps its signature and adds these rules: a non-.gd file maps through the scripts/scenes that reference it to their tests; a .gd maps to its direct tests plus the direct tests of its one-hop dependents; dev/** with no mentioning test maps to nothing (layers lint guarantees shipped code never reaches dev); tests/scenarios|golden|parity map to no unit tests; support/schemas/project.godot/addons stay FULL; an unreferenced asset stays FULL. Full transitive closure was measured and rejected: 563 of 611 shipped files reach >= 80% of the suite through the composition root. `--why` prints the chain for one test; `--history=N` replays git history through the map, so the claim stays measurable.

## Flow
- agent edits a png, a table row or a dev bench file and runs `run_unit --changed`
- today: 'FULL suite: ...: no test mentions it', ~50 s of GUT on every fast file
- after: the scripts that load it -> their tests, plus a note naming the reach; `--why` explains any pick
- tools/mutate picks the same, better-scoped tests automatically

## Expected impact
FULL fallbacks drop from 57% to 24% of commits touching project/. Mean files selected drops 200 -> 94, even with the one-hop safety added. Each FULL avoided saves ~50 s of GUT (the last full gut step: 53.5 s). The one-hop rule closes a measured under-selection where `--changed` stays green and the full gate goes red.

## Evaluation
Claim: reach-aware mapping avoids most FULL fallbacks and stops missing the tests of direct dependents.
Before: last 600 non-merge commits, 157 touch project/ (non-.uid/.import/.md); current test_map sends 90 (57%) to FULL, mean 200.0 test files per commit. 420 of the 473 directly mapped shipped .gd files have one-hop dependents whose tests are not selected (5,945 missed file edges). Example: core/clock/sim_loop.gd -> 1 test while 7 source files use SimLoop.
After: same replay with the rules simulated: 38 FULL (24%), mean 94.3 files, 6 commits correctly need 0 unit tests (dev-only).
Method: simulation - scratch probe sim.mjs imports the real mapChanges/realIndex and replays `git log --no-merges -n 600 --name-only` through the current and the proposed rules on the current tree index.
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: Probe output (scratchpad/probe/sim.mjs): current {commits:157, full:90, pctFull:57, meanFiles:200.0} top reasons features/characters 27 (pngs), data/tables 14, features/vehicles 8, dev/bench 6, data/schemas 6; reach+1hop {full:38, pctFull:24, zero:6, meanFiles:94.3}. map2.mjs: 138/611 shipped .gd map FULL today (incl. core/save/save.gd, core/log/log.gd, core/world_system.gd); directMapped 473, missFiles 420, miss 5945 (top: core/data/data_table.gd 18 direct vs +151 via dependents; core/clock/sim_clock.gd 56 vs +142). Full transitive closure: 563/611 files >= 80% of 346 test files (rejected). CLI today: `node tools/tests/test_map.mjs project/data/tables/bosses.json` -> 'FULL suite: ... no test mentions it'; project/dev/bench/bench_driver.gd -> FULL; project/core/clock/sim_loop.gd -> 1 test (test_quest_objectives). Lane: docs/day/2026-11-07/city/JOURNAL.md:643 a table change ran 1504 tests via --changed's FULL fallback; docs/day/2026-11-06/chars/JOURNAL.md:450 'unit (full, via --changed: schema touched)'.

title: run_unit triage: cause, reach-from-your-diff verdict, rerun cmd per failure
acceptance: parseJunit on a fixture testcase whose failure CDATA is 'Unexpected Errors:\n[1] <engine>!actions.custom_samplers.has(tex_builtin)\n[2] <engine>Parameter "t" is null' -> case.cause = the two error lines, and the digest line carries them (today: message 'Unexpected Errors:' with no cause)

logSlice(fixtureLog, 'res://tests/unit/test_save_slots.gd', 'test_unwritable_profile_reports_and_does_not_throw') -> the 'ERROR: Could not create directory ...' line, its 'at:' line and the first GDScript backtrace frame; stops at the next '* test_' line or file header; returns [] for a test with no engine output

triage(failure in tests/unit/test_vehicle_view.gd, changed=['project/features/vehicles/vehicle_glow.gdshader'], fixture index where vehicle_view.gd references the shader) -> verdict 'REACHED by project/features/vehicles/vehicle_glow.gdshader'; with changed=['project/features/hud/hud_feed.gd'] that does not reach it -> verdict 'UNREACHED: none of your 1 changed file(s) reaches this test - suspect the base or the machine'
every triage block ends with a paste-ready command 'node tools/tests/run_unit.mjs --select=test_vehicle_view --test=test_glow_is_lit' (exact basename and function from the junit case)

parseArgs(['--failed']) -> o.failed=true; buildPlan with a previous build/test-results/unit-tests.junit.xml holding failures in 2 files -> files = those 2 files; with no previous report -> UsageError 'no previous unit run to re-run' (exit 2)
a run whose log has 'SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error ...' + 'at: res://tests/unit/test_x.gd:12' -> a triage entry with verdict 'PARSE' naming res://tests/unit/test_x.gd:12 (the file GUT silently skipped)

after a red run build/test-results/unit-triage.json exists with schema 'gtai.unit-triage/1' and one entry per failure {file,line,name,message,cause[],verdict,reach[],flakes,rerun}; a green run removes a stale one
a failing test with 2 entries in the flake ledger (GTAI_FLAKES_FILE fixture) -> the block says 'flaked 2x before (last <ts>, <lanes>)' and the run still fails
premise: tools/tests/junit.mjs:26 - the digest keeps only the first line of the failure text
project/addons/gut/gut.gd:625 - GUT's engine-error failure is 'Unexpected Errors:\n' + one line per error, so the cause is on line 2+, which the digest drops
project/addons/gut/error_tracker.gd:157 - each error line is '<type>code', the actual engine message
tools/tests/run_unit.mjs:188 - a red run prints 'FAIL <file:line> name - message' and only a log pointer (:190) to a 5,321-line, 205 KB log
tools/tests/run_unit.mjs:35 - parseArgs has no way to re-run the last failures; the agent rebuilds --select/--test by hand
tools/tests/test_map.mjs:21 - the runner already holds the diff->test map it needs to say whether the agent's change can reach a failing test, and never uses it after a failure
docs/day/2026-11-07/vehicles/JOURNAL.md:284 - 6 FAILED all 'Unexpected Errors'; the cause (!actions.custom_samplers.has(tex_builtin)) had to be dug out of the log
rollback: Revert the series: triage.mjs is new and only called from report(); junit.mjs keeps message as is and adds cause[] (additive); --failed is a new flag, so removing it breaks no existing call.
runner_up: `run_unit --base`: re-run the failing files at the merge-base in a temp worktree (reusing tools/mutate's worktree code) to prove pre-existing vs mine - decisive but ~40 s of import per use; better as a follow-up once UNREACHED verdicts show how often it is needed.
body:
## Summary
After a red unit run an agent gets one line per failure, and for engine errors that line has no cause ('Unexpected Errors:'). Turn the red summary into a triage block per failure: the real cause lines, a verdict on whether the agent's own diff reaches the test, the flake history, and a paste-ready rerun command. Add `--failed` to re-run exactly the last failures.

## Description
junit.mjs keeps the full failure text and exposes `cause` (GUT's numbered error lines). The new triage.mjs (a) slices unit-tests.log by GUT's own 'res://file' / '* test_name' headers to attach the engine ERROR + at: + first backtrace frame for that test; (b) runs test_map over the same changed files `--changed` uses and prints REACHED by <path> / UNREACHED / PARSE; (c) reads the flake ledger for that test; (d) builds the rerun command. run_unit writes build/test-results/unit-triage.json (gtai.unit-triage/1) for agents to read instead of grepping the log. `--failed` reads the previous junit and runs only the failing files with the failing test name.

## Flow
- today: FAIL line -> open the 205 KB log -> find '* test_name' -> read the ERROR under it -> git diff and guess whether it is mine -> hand-write --select/--test -> re-run
- after: read one block (cause, REACHED/UNREACHED, flaked Nx, rerun cmd) -> `run_unit --failed`

## Expected impact
A red run's diagnosis goes from ~5 manual steps to reading one block. The 'is this mine?' call stops being blind: the runner already holds the diff-to-test map. Agents get a machine-readable triage file instead of log greps.

## Evaluation
Claim: the runner's red output carries the cause and the mine-or-not signal it already has the data for.
Before: for an engine-error failure the digest message is 'Unexpected Errors:' (0 cause lines). Diagnosis needs the 5,321-line / 205 KB build/test-results/unit-tests.log, and no mode re-runs the last failures. Measured on the current log: the save test's engine ERROR sits 1 line under its '* test_unwritable_profile_reports_and_does_not_throw' header, so it can be attributed.
After: the same failure prints its error lines inline plus a verdict and a rerun command; `--failed` re-runs it in one command.
Method: probe - read junit.mjs:26 against gut.gd:625/error_tracker.gd:157 (cause on line 2+); grepped the live unit-tests.log for per-test headers ('res://...' then '* test_') and ERROR placement (lines 1766-1771, 4374-4379).
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: junit.mjs:26 `c.message = text.split('\n')[0].trim()`; gut.gd:625 `script_inst._fail(str("Unexpected Errors:\n", error_tracker.get_fail_text_for_errors(test_id)))`; error_tracker.gd:157 `error_texts.append(str('<', error.get_error_type_name(), '>', error.code))`. build/test-results/unit-tests.log: 5321 lines, sections '===== import (exit 0, 33.6 s)', '===== gut (exit 0, 53.5 s)'; per-file header line 1766 'res://tests/unit/test_aim_reach.gd' then '* test_...' lines; line 4376-4378 '* test_unwritable_profile_reports_and_does_not_throw' / 'ERROR: Could not create directory ...' / 'at: make_dir_recursive'. Lane cost: docs/day/2026-11-07/vehicles/JOURNAL.md:284-285 (6 FAILED 'Unexpected Errors', cause found by hand); docs/night/2026-11-05/look/JOURNAL.md:306 and docs/night/2026-11-05/ranged/JOURNAL.md:1915 (known-flake judgement made from memory, re-ran the whole suite). Flake ledger today: 2 entries (`node tools/tests/flakes.mjs report --min=2`).
